9958dcfe79c7dcfa9657bf6710ac6433077bb4fa.summary: Silent Push Threat Team blog (published 2024-10-02) on FIN7, described as a financially motivated group with ties to Russia. FIN7 is said to run at least seven fake 'AI deepnude' generator sites and 'free download' and 'free trial' honeypots that deliver Redline Stealer, D3F@ck Loader and Lumma Stealer. A separate malvertising campaign pushes NetSupport RAT through fake browser-extension pages that lead to .MSIX malware. The report describes SEO tactics and shell websites, and says the sites found were taken offline after takedown requests. Silent Push counts 4,000+ FIN7 domains and IPs.…

996cbdff883d200909484667f098b59aa60e31b0.summary: BleepingComputer, citing Cybereason Nocturnus Team research, reports that APT35, described as an Iranian state-backed group, is deploying a new PowerShell-based backdoor called PowerLess along with info stealers and keyloggers. The researchers found potential connections to Memento ransomware, which the report says has been active since April 2021 and has targeted VMware vCenter servers. The article also cites a November joint advisory from US and UK agencies and Microsoft's tracking of six Iranian threat groups using ransomware.

99413f03171db34e715c6c04b5644af977996e87.summary: Mandiant's M-Trends 2024 special report summarises its 2023 incident response investigations. It reports exploits as the most common initial access route (38% of intrusions where the vector was identified), median dwell time falling to 10 days, and financially motivated intrusions rising to 36%. It highlights zero-day exploitation of file transfer and email gateway appliances (MOVEit, Barracuda ESG), China-nexus custom malware for edge devices and hypervisors, and ransomware groups such as ALPHV and LOCKBIT. It also covers threat groups, malware and ATT&CK technique frequencies.

hedges: Attributions to suspected Chinese espionage groups (e.g. UNC4841, UNC3886) are stated as suspected, not confirmed.
Mandiant says it believes APT43 funds itself through cyber crime; the report presents this as belief, not established fact.
The report says the fall in BEACON usage could align with several explanations, offered as possibilities rather than findings.
The fall in observed malware families may reflect tool reuse or compromises that use no malware; the report does not establish this.
Data leak site listings are described as skewed toward victims who refused to pay, so they are useful only for broad trends.
Motivation could not be determined with high confidence for 36% of threat clusters.
Metrics are based only on Mandiant Consulting investigations from 2023, and victim information has been sanitized.
The government sector decline is said to potentially reflect fewer Ukraine-war-related investigations, a possibility rather than a finding.
